The response should not use anything other than pins from the 'Recipes' board to identify the past dietary restriction. The response should state that the user is no longer following the vegetarian dietary restriction.

The response should mention that the user's recent saves confirm the restriction is not current. For example, it could reference the current saves from the "Today" and "2 months ago" history, which include: "Grilled Steak Fajita Roll-Ups Recipe with Asparagus" (today), "Crunchy Chicken Salad Cucumber Roll Ups" (2 months ago), and "Easy Chicken Tom Yum Soup" (2 months ago).
The response should state that the user has not been vegetarian for at least 2 years.

The response should cite the Pinterest history from 2 years ago as evidence that the restriction has not been active for at least 2 years. For example, it could specifically note the presence of meat-based pins such as: "Deliciously Creamy Garlic Mushrooms with Bacon are a fabulous side dish prepared with butter, garlic, bacon, and cream", "PINEAPPLE TERIYAKI CHICKEN MEATBALLS", "Pesto Chicken with Tortellini and Veggies (Asparagus, Cherry Tomatoes)", and/or "Sausage and Veggies Skillet with Bell Peppers, Zucchini, and Corn-30 Minute, One-Pan Meal"

The response should not cite anything other than the user's profile history to support its claim that the user is not currently vegetarian. For example, it should not reference any Pinterest boards such as "Recipes" or "Shtuff" in this section.

The response should explicitly state that 2 years is the maximum verifiable duration. For example, it could explain that because the provided timestamped history only goes back exactly 2 years, it is impossible to determine exactly when the transition away from the diet occurred prior to that cutoff.
